title: Fischer vs Spassky, Game 6
summary: Game 6 of the 1972 World Championship match in Reykjavik is widely remembered as a turning point, with Fischer's win ending in a kingside attack after a quiet opening. Watch how the position stays level until Black's 20...d4 gives White a clear space advantage, and how the f-pawn and rook lift decide the game.

moves.comment: 1.c4 is a flexible flank opening that stakes a claim in the centre without committing. The engine slightly prefers 1.e4, but the evaluation barely moves.
1...e6 prepares ...d5 and keeps Black's pawn structure solid. The engine prefers 1...e5, but this is a sound choice.
2.Nf3 develops the knight and keeps options open. The engine prefers 2.d4 immediately, though the difference is small.
2...d5 challenges the centre directly and is the engine's top choice. It keeps the position level.
3.d4 builds a classical pawn centre and is the engine's first choice. White keeps a slight, harmless edge.
3...Nf6 develops naturally, but the engine prefers 3...dxc4 to resolve the tension before White can build up.
4.Nc3 adds a defender to the centre and develops a piece. It is the engine's best move.
4...Be7 is playable but passive. The engine prefers 4...Bb4 to pin the knight and create counterplay.
5.Bg5 pins the knight and pressures Black's centre. The engine prefers 5.Bf4, but the pin is a reasonable try.
5...O-O completes Black's development and gets the king safe. The engine prefers 5...h6 first, but this is still fine.
6.e3 opens the c1 bishop, supports d4 and solidifies White's position. It is the engine's best move.
6...h6 asks the bishop to decide its path. The engine prefers 6...Nbd7 to develop first, though the move is sound.
7.Bh4 keeps the bishop on the diagonal and avoids being exchanged. It is the engine's best move.
7...b6 prepares ...Bb7 and gives the light-squared bishop a useful diagonal. It is the engine's best move.
8.cxd5 releases the central tension. The engine prefers 8.Rc1 to keep more pressure, but the position stays level.
8...Nxd5 recaptures with the knight and centralises it. It is the engine's best move.
9.Bxe7 trades bishops and simplifies the position. It is the engine's best move.
9...Qxe7 recaptures and keeps the queen active on the e-file. It is the engine's best move.
10.Nxd5 trades knights and opens the centre. The engine prefers 10.Rc1, but the move is still reasonable.
10...exd5 recaptures and opens the e-file. It is the engine's best move and keeps the balance.
11.Rc1 places the rook on the open c-file. It is the engine's best move and a natural plan.
11...Be6 develops the bishop and contests the centre. It is the engine's best move.
12.Qa4 leaves the queen somewhat exposed. The engine prefers 12.Bd3, though the position stays equal.
12...c5 strikes at the centre and challenges d4. It is the engine's best move.
13.Qa3 keeps the queen on the long diagonal and eyes Black's position. It is the engine's best move.
13...Rc8 contests the open c-file with the rook. It is the engine's best move.
14.Bb5 is an active try, though the engine prefers 14.Be2. The evaluation tips slightly towards Black.
14...a6 kicks the bishop and gains queenside space. The engine prefers 14...Qb7, though the move is sound.
15.dxc5 clarifies the centre and opens files. It is the engine's best move.
15...bxc5 recaptures and opens the b-file. It is the engine's best move.
16.O-O castles and connects the rooks. It is the engine's best move.
16...Ra7 lifts the rook to defend along the seventh rank. The engine prefers 16...Qb7, but the move is playable.
17.Be2 consolidates the bishop and prepares to link the rooks. It is the engine's best move.
17...Nd7 brings the knight towards the centre. The engine prefers 17...a5, but the move is still sound.
18.Nd4 centralises the knight and eyes the c6 and e6 squares. It is the engine's best move.
18...Qf8 is a slightly passive queen move. The engine prefers 18...a5, though the position remains balanced.
19.Nxe6 trades the knight for the bishop and opens the f-file. It is the engine's best move.
19...fxe6 recaptures and opens the f-file for Black's rook. It is the engine's best move.
20.e4 builds a central pawn wedge and gains space. It is the engine's best move.
20...d4 is a mistake. It gives White a clear space advantage, and the engine prefers 20...dxe4 instead.

moment.title: Black's premature 20...d4 push
moment.text: After 20.e4 Black advances the pawn to d4 instead of capturing. The engine prefers 20...dxe4, and the evaluation jumps from +0.3 to +1.5. This gives White a lasting space advantage and a bind on the kingside.

moves.comment: 21.f4 supports the e5 push and grabs more space. It is the engine's best move and builds a strong bind.
21...Qe7 is a defensive regrouping. The engine prefers 21...Nb6, though the position is already difficult.
22.e5 gains more space and cramps Black's pieces. The engine prefers 22.Qh3, though the move is still good.
22...Rb8 is a mistake that worsens Black's position. The engine prefers 22...Nb6 to challenge the advance.

moment.title: 22...Rb8 allows f5 and e5 to bite
moment.text: Black's rook move leaves the queenside passive while White's e5 advance cramps the position. The engine prefers 22...Nb6 to challenge the advance, but after the rook move the evaluation rises to +2.4. The plan of attack becomes clear.

moves.comment: 23.Bc4 places the bishop on the long diagonal aimed at the king. It is the engine's best move.
23...Kh8 steps the king off the diagonal. It is the engine's best move.
24.Qh3 brings the queen to the kingside to join the attack. It is the engine's best move.
24...Nf8 is an inaccuracy that retreats the knight. The engine prefers 24...Rxb2, and White's advantage grows.

moment.title: 24...Nf8 retreats instead of counterattacking
moment.text: Black's knight retreat to f8 is an inaccuracy that lets White consolidate. The engine prefers 24...Rxb2, and the evaluation moves from +2.1 to +3.4. White's build-up continues with a simple plan.

moves.comment: 25.b3 solidifies the queenside and secures c4. It is the engine's best move.
25...a5 creates counterplay on the queenside. It is the engine's best move.
26.f5 opens lines against the king. The engine prefers 26.a4, though the advance is still good.
26...exf5 recaptures and opens the e-file. The engine prefers 26...Qg5, though the move is playable.
27.Rxf5 brings the rook into the attack. It is the engine's best move.
27...Nh7 reroutes the knight to defend. The engine prefers 27...a4, though the move is playable.
28.Rcf1 doubles rooks on the f-file. It is the engine's best move and increases the pressure.
28...Qd8 is a passive regroup. The engine prefers 28...a4, and White's advantage grows.
29.Qg3 brings the queen into the attack on the kingside. The engine prefers 29.e6, but the move is still good.
29...Re7 defends the seventh rank. The engine prefers 29...a4, though the move is playable.
30.h4 advances on the kingside to prepare h5. The engine prefers 30.e6, though the move is still good.
30...Rbb7 is an inaccuracy that adds little defence. The engine prefers 30...d3, and the evaluation rises for White.
31.e6 pushes the pawn deep into Black's position. It is the engine's best move.
31...Rbc7 defends the seventh rank. The engine prefers 31...Qb8, though the move is playable.
32.Qe5 centralises the queen and pressures the position. The engine prefers 32.R1f3, though the move is good.
32...Qe8 is a slight retreat. The engine prefers 32...d3, and the balance continues to tilt towards White.
33.a4 restricts Black's queenside play. The engine prefers 33.R5f3, though the move is still good.
33...Qd8 is the engine's best move, reorganising the queen.
34.R1f2 doubles rooks on the f-file. The engine prefers 34.Bd3, though the move is good.
34...Qe8 shuffles the queen. The engine prefers 34...d3, and the evaluation continues to rise for White.
35.R2f3 adds a second rook to the f-file. The engine prefers 35.Rf1, though the move is still good.
35...Qd8 is a passive move. The engine prefers 35...Rb7, and the evaluation favours White.
36.Bd3 places the bishop on a useful diagonal. The engine prefers 36.Rh5, though the move is good.
36...Qe8 shuffles the queen again. The engine prefers 36...Qg8, and the advantage grows for White.
37.Qe4 centralises the queen to support the attack. The engine prefers 37.Rf7, though the move is good.
37...Nf6 offers the knight to open the kingside. It is the engine's best move, though it gives White a material decision.

moment.title: 37...Nf6 offers the knight to open lines
moment.text: After a long build-up, Black's knight is sacrificed to open the kingside. The engine rates it as the best move, but the position is already close to decisive. The sacrifice is part of a plan that Black cannot easily stop.

moves.comment: 38.Rxf6 accepts the sacrifice and opens lines. It is the engine's best move.
38...gxf6 recaptures and exposes Black's king. It is the engine's best move.
39.Rxf6 brings the second rook into the attack. It is the engine's best move.
39...Kg8 steps the king to the back rank. The engine prefers 39...c4, though the position is lost.
40.Bc4 brings the bishop back onto the long diagonal. It is the engine's best move.
40...Kh8 returns the king, but the engine now sees mate. The engine prefers 40...Rb7, though the position is already lost.
41.Qf4 keeps the attack going and the engine shows mate in seven. The game ends 1-0 with White's win.

moment.title: 41.Qf4 and mate in seven
moment.text: White's queen move keeps the attack going, and the engine evaluates the position as mate in seven. The game ends 1-0 with White's win. Watch how the queen and rooks combine on the kingside.

lessons: Look for a space advantage before you go for a direct attack, because a clamp like f4 and e5 can restrict the opponent's pieces.
Before advancing a pawn, check whether a capture keeps the tension and whether the advance gives the opponent targets.
When the opponent sacrifices, check the resulting open files and count the attackers before you accept.
